jmdict.name: JMdict (English)
jmdict.note: This is the hash src/data/generated/word-definitions.json records for the JMdict it was cut from, not the hash of what the URL serves today. EDRDG rebuilds JMdict daily and keeps only the current build, so this exact archive cannot be downloaded again. Every JMdict ingest therefore stops today, which is the intent: a JMdict re-cut is always a deliberate upgrade, never something to let happen by accident. Rerun with --accept-source to record the current build and cut against it, and expect the reduction to move.
jmdict.versionFrom: the date word-definitions.json was last refreshed (commit 7f7cc3d8); the archive's own creation date was not written down at the time

scripts/ingest/cejc_reading_frequency.py.note: The CEJC archive on disk is the one this file records for itself, byte for byte. Re-running the pass today still moves three counts (ちち 50 to 684, ちゃん 4268 to 4273, one core category count 2 to 7), because the pass also reads word-definitions.json and that was refreshed on 2026-08-29, after this file was last cut. The archive is pinned; the staleness is against a committed input, not against CEJC.

scripts/ingest/jmdict_word_definitions.p.note: Read off the source block word-definitions.json carries, not stamped by a run: the pinned JMdict is no longer downloadable, so this pass stops today. Against the JMdict of 2026-09-13 the reduction gains 2 words (かみそり, 公平) and changes 9 (と, なり, 大小, 大気, 寂しい, 最後, 発電, 硬い, 進む), all of them upstream sense edits, none of them a defect in the ingest.

note: Which upstream archive each ingest under scripts/ingest reads, and the exact bytes it read. archives is the pin; builtFrom is one entry per ingest pass; unpinned names every generated file the pin does not reach and says why. See scripts/ingest/sources.mjs for the mechanism and src/data/source-manifest.test.ts for what is enforced.

confusable-derived.json.why: Cut from a JMdict, a KANJIDIC2 and a KRADFILE whose hashes nobody wrote down at the time, and EDRDG serves only the current build, so those exact archives cannot be recovered. Re-cutting against today's JMdict would move the word set, the ranks and the fact ids a learner's study history is stored under, which is a content decision and not this one. The pin arrives the next time the file is deliberately re-cut, which now takes --accept-source.

grammar-corpus-meta.json.why: Cut from a Tatoeba snapshot of 248,802 Japanese sentences; the export has grown since and Tatoeba publishes no archive of past days, so that snapshot cannot be recovered. A re-cut re-selects every one of the 50-odd patterns from different sentences and moves the pinned post-audit counts, so it is a deliberate act and now takes --accept-source. The three current exports are pinned in archives above, so the next re-cut is recorded.

kanji-etymology.json.why: Parsed from English Wiktionary page by page over the live API, throttled and cached. There is no archive to hash: the upstream is 2,136 pages, each with its own revision, and Wiktionary publishes no dump this ingest reads. Pinning it means recording a revision id per page, which is its own piece of work.
